title: Send a prescription vial by hospital pneumatic tube: vial in the carrier, swivel lid shut, carrier up into the station
instruction: Send this prescription vial to the ward by tube: put it in the carrier, swing the carrier's lid shut until it catches, then push the carrier up into the station's send tube until the station takes it, and let go.
context: Much hospital medication moves by pneumatic tube. One maker's tube system "is used in over 80% of hospitals in North America" (Health-ISAC, 2021); the US has 6,100 hospitals (AHA, 2026). "pharmaceuticals account for 30%" of what hospital tube systems carry, and one university hospital's system completes "more than 6,000 transactions on an average day" (MIT Technology Review, 2024). The tubes move a carrier by themselves, but someone loads and sends every one, so that is the step a robot must take over to automate medication transport. NHS design guidance (SHTM 08-04 Part B) gives the rule scored here: "The carrier lids should be of the swivel pattern designed so that the lid is positively secured before loading the carrier into the system (an insecure lid may be dislodged by the system)." The carrier stands on a small end, so one hand holds it while the other swings the lid shut; then it goes up into a tube only slightly wider than itself.
setup: Cm from the midpoint between the arm bases, x away from the robot, y left; heights above the table, which stands in for a 90 cm pharmacy counter. Wall, fixed: a board 2 cm thick at x 55 to 57, y -38 to 22, 66 high. Tube station on the wall, fixed: a bottom-loading station for a 110 mm line. Its send tube (grey PVC, 110 mm outside, 105.4 mm bore) hangs with its axis at x 41.0, y -8.0; at its lower end an entry collar 2 cm tall widens to 13.2 cm across at its lower edge, which is 30.0 up (1.2 m above the floor, the height NHS guidance gives for bottom-loading stations). Above the collar a grey cabinet 21.5 (x) by 22 (y) by 26 cm, underside 34 up, with a display on its front. For real trials without a working tube system, the README ("Building a bench station") specifies a low-cost stand-in: a 30 cm length of the line's 110 mm tube on a wall board with a sprung catch that holds a carrier pushed 7 cm up it. The station already has its destination and is waiting for a carrier. Carrier, loose: a short swivel-lid carrier for a 110 mm line, clear blue polycarbonate, 22.8 cm long, 10.4 cm across its two black hook-and-loop rings, 8.6 cm across its body between them, 8.0 cm bore, 290 g with its lid. It stands on its closed end, axis at x 27.0, y -8.0 (layout B: 28.5, -6.5). Its dark blue lid (8.8 cm across, 1.2 cm thick) turns on a pin beside the rim, on the carrier's left side, and starts swung 80 degrees open toward the robot. Its catch is a snap: about 0.7 N at the lid's far edge pushes it past a bump 5 degrees from shut, and the same opens it again. Vial, loose: a 13 dram amber prescription vial with a white child-resistant cap, 3.2 cm across, 6.9 cm tall, 30 g, standing at x 28.0, y 12.0 (B: 31.0, 10.0). Both arms start in their rest pose.
scoring: Scored at the end (a ruler, a side photo, the video). 0 unless the whole vial is inside the carrier (both its ends within the bore, between the closed end and the mouth's rim). Then 0.25. 0.5 if also the lid is secured: swung shut to within 3 degrees, where its catch holds it. 0.75 if also the carrier's top is in the station's send tube (2 cm or more above the entry collar's lower edge) but the station has not taken it, or a gripper is still within 3 cm of it, or it is still moving. 1.0: the station has taken the carrier (its top 7 cm up the send tube, on the tube's axis), both grippers are at least 3 cm from it, and it is at rest (under 2 cm/s). The whole trial scores 0 if the carrier's top ever enters the send tube (1 cm above the collar's lower edge) with the lid not secured, or if the vial or the carrier falls off the counter (5 cm below its top). Doing nothing scores 0.
reset_notes: Take the carrier out of the send tube and the vial out of the carrier, swing the lid open to its stop, and stand both on their marks. Nothing is consumed.
fidelity: Rigid parts at full size. Two things are rules, not contact physics: the lid's catch (a torque on its pin: a bump, then held) and the station's take-up (a carrier whose top is 7 cm up the send tube, on its axis, is held there). The rings' pile is not modelled: they are rigid, 101 mm across. Estimates: the carrier's wall, weight, ring places, lid, pin and catch; the station's collar, cabinet and take-up depth; the tube's bore. No bag or padding round the vial.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0; demo: 1.0 (the demo video and the setup picture show the overhead camera beside the left wrist camera; the wrist view in the setup picture was taken with the left arm moved aside)
